From 861ce4a3244c21b0af64f880d5bfe5e6e2fb9e4a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Laura Abbott <labbott@redhat.com>
Date: Mon, 8 May 2017 14:23:16 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] x86/mm/32: Set the '__vmalloc_start_set' flag in
 initmem_init()

'__vmalloc_start_set' currently only gets set in initmem_init() when
!CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES. This breaks detection of vmalloc address
with virt_addr_valid() with CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES=y, causing
a kernel crash:

  [mm/usercopy] 517e1fbeb6: kernel BUG at arch/x86/mm/physaddr.c:78!

Set '__vmalloc_start_set' appropriately for that case as well.

Reported-by: kbuild test robot <fengguang.wu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Laura Abbott <labbott@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Fixes: dc16ecf7fd1f ("x86-32: use specific __vmalloc_start_set flag in __virt_addr_valid")
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/1494278596-30373-1-git-send-email-labbott@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/x86/mm/numa_32.c b/arch/x86/mm/numa_32.c
index 6b7ce6279133..aca6295350f3 100644
--- a/arch/x86/mm/numa_32.c
+++ b/arch/x86/mm/numa_32.c
@@ -100,5 +100,6 @@ void __init initmem_init(void)
 	printk(KERN_DEBUG "High memory starts at vaddr %08lx\n",
 			(ulong) pfn_to_kaddr(highstart_pfn));
 
+	__vmalloc_start_set = true;
 	setup_bootmem_allocator();
 }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/mm/numa_32.c`**
   - A new line was added in the `initmem_init()` function to set the `__vmalloc_start_set` flag to `true`. This change ensures that the flag is set regardless of the `CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES` configuration, addressing a bug related to virtual address validation.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `numa_32.c` directly addresses a bug that occurs when `CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES` is enabled. By setting the `__vmalloc_start_set` flag in all cases, the patch ensures that the `virt_addr_valid()` function can correctly detect the vmalloc address, preventing kernel crashes that were previously triggered by the lack of this flag being set under certain configurations. This change is a fix for the issue reported by the kbuild test robot, which indicated a kernel bug related to address validation.

Reported-by: kbuild test robot <fengguang.wu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Laura Abbott <labbott@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Fixes: dc16ecf7fd1f ("x86-32: use specific __vmalloc_start_set flag in __virt_addr_valid")
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/1494278596-30373-1-git-send-email-labbott@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `__vmalloc_start_set` flag is only set when `!CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES`, leading to incorrect detection of vmalloc addresses when `CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES` is enabled. This results in the `virt_addr_valid()` function failing to validate virtual addresses correctly, causing a kernel crash.

Here is the patch:
 
 void __init initmem_init(void)
 {
 	x86_numa_init();
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_HIGHMEM
 	highstart_pfn = highend_pfn = max_pfn;
 	if (max_pfn > max_low_pfn)
 		highstart_pfn = max_low_pfn;
 	printk(KERN_NOTICE "%ldMB HIGHMEM available.\n",
 	       pages_to_mb(highend_pfn - highstart_pfn));
 	high_memory = (void *) __va(highstart_pfn * PAGE_SIZE - 1) + 1;
 #else
 	high_memory = (void *) __va(max_low_pfn * PAGE_SIZE - 1) + 1;
 #endif
 	printk(KERN_NOTICE "%ldMB LOWMEM available.\n",
 			pages_to_mb(max_low_pfn));
 	printk(KERN_DEBUG "max_low_pfn = %lx, highstart_pfn = %lx\n",
 			max_low_pfn, highstart_pfn);
 
 	printk(KERN_DEBUG "Low memory ends at vaddr %08lx\n",
 			(ulong) pfn_to_kaddr(max_low_pfn));
 
 	printk(KERN_DEBUG "High memory starts at vaddr %08lx\n",
 			(ulong) pfn_to_kaddr(highstart_pfn));
 
+	__vmalloc_start_set = true;
 	setup_bootmem_allocator();
 }
--

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (!CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES)
    __vmalloc_start_set = true;
```
Reason:
The `__vmalloc_start_set` flag is only set when `CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES` is not defined, which means that when `CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES` is enabled, the flag remains unset. This leads to incorrect behavior in the `virt_addr_valid()` function, which relies on this flag to validate virtual addresses, ultimately causing a kernel crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
__vmalloc_start_set = true;
```
Reason:
By unconditionally setting the `__vmalloc_start_set` flag to true in the `initmem_init()` function, the patch ensures that the flag is correctly set regardless of the `CONFIG_NEED_MULTIPLE_NODES` configuration. This allows the `virt_addr_valid()` function to properly validate virtual addresses, preventing the kernel crash.
